userStories.title: Refuse unhostable thread creates and mode changes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Refuse thread create and mode changes with a cause-specific 409 when enrolled runners cannot host the permanent kind/mode/backend combination.

**Motivation** — A thread that misses one is accepted (201) and its first turn queues forever with `stateReason = null`.

**Approach** —
- New `threadCapabilityMisfit(thread: PlacementThread, capabilities: RunnerCapabilities): ThreadCapabilityMisfit | null` in `placement-rules.ts`, with `type ThreadCapabilityMisfit = 'project_threads' | 'workspace_threads' | 'thread_modes' | 'thread_backend' | 'thread_write'`. It runs placement's capability-only thread rules in `firstMisfit`'s order: `kind === 'PROJECT'` without `projectThreads === true` gives `project_threads`; `kind === 'WORKSPACE'` without `workspaceThreads === true` gives `workspace_threads`; for `action` SESSION (absent means SESSION), `mode` `ask` or `full` without `threadModes === true` gives `thread_modes`, then `!servesThreadBackend(...)` gives `thread_backend`; for any other action, `threadWrite !== true` gives `thread_write`.
- `firstMisfit` (`placement-rules.ts:169`)
  - Baseline: the thread branch checks the five rules inline (lines 181-191).
  - Target: after `threads_disabled` and `protocol`, it returns `threadCapabilityMisfit(job.thread, runner.capabilities)` when that is non-null, then `trust_domain` and `thread_capacity` as today. Same results for every input.
- `ChatThreadRepository.anyRunnerServesBackend(backend)` (`apps/api/src/fleet/threads/domain/chat-thread.domain.ts:147`)
  - Baseline: `anyRunnerServesBackend(backend: ThreadBackend): Promise<boolean>`.
  - Target: `threadServeMisfit(need: ThreadServeNeed): Promise<ThreadCapabilityMisfit | null>`, with `interface ThreadServeNeed { backend: ThreadBackend; kind: ChatThreadKind; mode: ThreadMode; runnerId?: string | null; modesOnly?: true }`. `PrismaChatThreadRepository` reads `runner` rows with `enabled: true` and `protocolVersion >= THREAD_MIN_PROTOCOL_VERSION`, or, when `runnerId` is a string, only that runner's row (any `enabled` value; a missing row means nothing to judge). No rows: `null` (the #399 "fleet not set up" rule). Otherwise each row is judged with `threadCapabilityMisfit({ backend, kind, mode, enabled: true, action: 'SESSION' }, capabilities)`, or, when `modesOnly` is set, only by the mode rule (`mode` `ask`/`full` and `threadModes !== true` gives `thread_modes`, anything else `null`), so a backend change on the runner never refuses a mode change; any `null` verdict gives `null`. When every row misfits, the answer is the misfit of the runner that got furthest, by placement order `project_threads` = `workspace_threads` < `thread_modes` < `thread_backend` (the latest-ordered misfit wins).
- `assertBackendServed(threads, backend)` (`apps/api/src/fleet/threads/thread-backend-served.ts:17`)
  - Target: `assertThreadServed(threads: Pick<ChatThreadRepository, 'threadServeMisfit'>, need: ThreadServeNeed): Promise<void>`. `null` returns. `thread_backend` throws `ConflictAppException(refusalArgs(backend), 'threads.backendUnavailable')` exactly as today; `project_threads` throws `ConflictAppException({}, 'threads.projectThreadsUnavailable')`; `workspace_threads` throws `ConflictAppException({}, 'threads.workspaceThreadsUnavailable')`; `thread_modes` throws `ConflictAppException({ mode }, 'threads.modeUnavailable')`. `thread_write` cannot occur (the need is always a SESSION); the switch is exhaustive, and an unexpected value throws `Error('unexpected thread misfit')`.
- `ThreadsService.assertBackendServed(backend)` and `WorkspaceThreadsService.assertBackendServed(backend)` become `assertThreadServed(need)`. `ThreadsService.create` calls it with `{ backend, kind: 'PROJECT', mode: 'read' }` for a PROJECT thread and `{ backend, kind: 'REPO', mode: normalized.mode }` for a REPO thread; `WorkspaceThreadsService.create` with `{ backend, kind: 'WORKSPACE', mode: 'read' }`. `ThreadsController.create` and `WorkspaceThreadsController.create` call it before the approval gate with the normalized kind, and mode `normalized.mode` for a REPO thread or `'read'` for a PROJECT or WORKSPACE thread, as #399 does for the backend.
- New `ThreadsService.assertModeServed(projectId: string, threadId: string, mode: ThreadMode): Promise<void>`: for `mode === 'read'` it returns; otherwise it loads the thread (`threads.notFound` 404 when missing), returns when `thread.kind !== 'REPO'` (so the existing 400 `threads.input` for a non-REPO ask/full still wins), and calls `assertThreadServed({ backend: thread.backend, kind: 'REPO', mode, runnerId: thread.runnerId, modesOnly: true })`. `ThreadsController.changeMode` calls it before the approval gate, and `ThreadsService.changeMode` calls it again before `this.threads.changeMode(...)`.
- i18n `apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/threads.json` gain `projectThreadsUnavailable`, `workspaceThreadsUnavailable` and `modeUnavailable` (`{mode}`), each with a `"409"` message. The 409 `@ApiResponse` descriptions on the create and mode routes name the new keys.

Thread create still accepts a thread when no thread-capable runner is enrolled (#399's "fleet not set up" rule). Capacity, budget, online state and labels are not judged at create: they are not permanent, and the thread page now explains them through `queuedTurn`. The mode check judges the thread's own runner when it has one, because every later turn is pinned to it (`pinnedRunnerId: thread.runnerId`). A thread that has not run yet is judged against the fleet.

**Scope** — In: pure placement extraction, repository/service/controller preflight, errors, fixture updates and `bun run generate` for OpenAPI/CLI. Out: dashboard judgements (US-002), detail queuedTurn (US-003), queued notice (US-004), and judging runner capacity, online state, labels or budget at thread create or mode change.

**Interface** — `threadCapabilityMisfit(thread: PlacementThread, capabilities: RunnerCapabilities): ThreadCapabilityMisfit | null`; `type ThreadCapabilityMisfit = 'project_threads' | 'workspace_threads' | 'thread_modes' | 'thread_backend' | 'thread_write'`; `interface ThreadServeNeed { backend: ThreadBackend; kind: ChatThreadKind; mode: ThreadMode; runnerId?: string | null; modesOnly?: true }`; `threadServeMisfit(need: ThreadServeNeed): Promise<ThreadCapabilityMisfit | null>`; `assertThreadServed(threads: Pick<ChatThreadRepository, 'threadServeMisfit'>, need: ThreadServeNeed): Promise<void>`; `ThreadsService.assertModeServed(projectId: string, threadId: string, mode: ThreadMode): Promise<void>`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] threadCapabilityMisfit for a PROJECT SESSION thread on capabilities that offer a native model but whose projectThreads is not true returns 'project_threads'.
[unit] threadCapabilityMisfit for a WORKSPACE SESSION thread on capabilities whose workspaceThreads is not true returns 'workspace_threads'.
[unit] threadCapabilityMisfit for a REPO SESSION in mode ask on capabilities whose threadModes is not true returns 'thread_modes'.

[unit] threadCapabilityMisfit for a REPO SESSION in mode read on the same capabilities, with a served backend, returns null; ThreadsService.assertModeServed(projectId, threadId, 'read') likewise returns without a capability refusal.
[unit] threadCapabilityMisfit for a REPO SESSION in mode full with threadModes: true and a backend model the capabilities do not offer returns 'thread_backend'.
[unit] assertThreadServed with a stub threadServeMisfit resolving 'project_threads' rejects with a 409 whose i18n key is threads.projectThreadsUnavailable.
[unit] assertThreadServed with the stub resolving 'workspace_threads' rejects with key threads.workspaceThreadsUnavailable.
[unit] assertThreadServed with the stub resolving 'thread_modes' for need mode full rejects with key threads.modeUnavailable and args { mode: 'full' }.

[integration] With the test Postgres and one enabled runner at protocol 4 that offers a native model but not projectThreads, POST /api/projects/:slug/threads for a PROJECT thread answers 409 with the threads.projectThreadsUnavailable message, and no thread row is persisted for that request.

[integration] With one enabled runner that offers the backend but not workspaceThreads, POST /api/threads for a WORKSPACE thread answers 409 with the threads.workspaceThreadsUnavailable message, and no thread row is persisted for that request.

[integration] With one enabled runner that offers the backend without threadModes, POST /api/projects/:slug/threads for a REPO thread in mode ask answers 409 with the threads.modeUnavailable message naming ask, and no thread row is persisted for that request.

[integration] With two enabled runners, one offering the backend without threadModes and one with threadModes: true that does not offer the backend, creating a REPO thread in mode full for that backend answers 409 with the threads.backendUnavailable message.
[integration] With no enabled runner at protocol 4 or later, POST /api/projects/:slug/threads for a PROJECT thread answers 201.

[integration] PATCH /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/mode with { mode: 'ask' } on a REPO thread whose runnerId names a runner without threadModes answers 409 with threads.modeUnavailable while another enabled runner has threadModes: true, and the thread's stored mode is unchanged.

[integration] PATCH /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id/mode with { mode: 'ask' } on a REPO thread whose runner has threadModes: true but no longer offers the thread's backend answers 200 (the mode check judges only threadModes).

userStories.title: Explain unplaceable THREAD jobs in the dashboard
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Judge queued THREAD jobs with the same placement rules and shared verdict classification as other jobs.

**Motivation** — `jobUnplaceableItems` (`apps/api/src/fleet/dashboard/attention-unplaceable.ts:64`) returns nothing for `isThreadKind(job.command)`, and the thread page shows the message as pending with no explanation.

**Approach** —
- New `apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/unplaceable-verdict.ts`:
  - `export const UNPLACEABLE_VERDICTS` and `export type UnplaceableVerdict`, moved unchanged from `dashboard.types.ts:102` (values `never`, `budget_paused`, `runners_paused`, `waiting_capacity`, `no_fit`, `no_runners`, `fits_not_placed`); `dashboard.types.ts` re-exports both, so `fleet-dashboard.dto.ts` and other importers keep working.
  - `export interface UnplaceableJudgement { verdict: UnplaceableVerdict; severity: 'error' | 'warning'; misfits: Array<{ runnerId: string; runnerName: string; reason: MisfitReason }> }`.
  - `export function judgeUnplaceable(input: { job: PlacementJob; scopePaused: boolean; pool: readonly PlacementRunner[]; loads: ReadonlyMap<string, RunnerLoad>; runnerPaused: (runnerId: string) => boolean; now: Date; offlineSec: number }): UnplaceableJudgement | null`. Order: `scopePaused` gives `budget_paused`/warning with no misfits; an empty `pool` gives `no_runners`/error; otherwise `evaluateRunners(...)`, and when some runner has `reason === null` the answer is `null` (delayed, not unplaceable). Misfits sort by `runnerName`, then `runnerId`. The classification is today's `classify`, with `thread_capacity` added to the waiting reasons (`capacity`, `busy_repo`, `trust_domain`, `thread_capacity`).
- `jobUnplaceableItems` (`attention-unplaceable.ts:64`)
  - Baseline: returns `[]` for `isThreadKind(job.command)`; classifies inline.
  - Target: a THREAD row with a `threadTurn` is judged like any other job, with `toPlacementJob(job, job, { ...job.threadTurn, enabled: input.threadsEnabled })`; a THREAD row with no `threadTurn` is skipped (placement skips such a broken row too). All rows go through `judgeUnplaceable`, and `RUNNER_FIXABLE_REASONS` handling stays.
- `DryRunInput` gains `threadsEnabled: boolean`; `DashboardService` passes `this.cfg.threadsEnabled`, and its `DashboardConfig` `Pick` (`dashboard.service.ts:12`) gains `'threadsEnabled'`.
- `DashboardJobRow` gains optional `threadTurn?: { backend: ThreadBackend; action: ThreadAction; kind: ChatThreadKind; mode: ThreadMode }`. `PrismaDashboardRepository.findQueuedWindow` fills it for THREAD rows from the job's `fleetThreadTurn` (`mode` absent means `read`, `backend`, `action`) and its thread's `kind` (`WORKSPACE`/`PROJECT`, otherwise `REPO`), the same mapping `findThreadAssign` uses.
- `DashboardRunnerRow` gains `protocolVersion: number` and `threadCapacity: number`, selected by `findRunners`; `toCandidate` copies both into the `PlacementRunner`.

Placement owns the thread rules. Create, mode change, the dashboard and thread detail all reach them through `threadCapabilityMisfit`, `evaluateRunners` and `judgeUnplaceable`, never a copy (`apps/api/CLAUDE.md` dashboard rule). Retain current classify priority: all permanent misfits -> never/error; all waiting reasons -> waiting_capacity/warning; all budget_paused -> runners_paused/warning; otherwise no_fit/warning. Preserve unreadable-capability exclusion, reason limits/totals, project scoping and scoped vault providers. Update dashboard fixture builders and select expectations.

**Scope** — In: shared pure judgement, dashboard rows/config/candidate mapping and real dashboard integration. Out: thread create/mode preflight (US-001), PlacementService.queuedVerdict and detail DTOs (US-003), and web queued notice (US-004). Writing `FleetJob.stateReason` for a queued THREAD job; the reason is computed on read (dashboard, thread detail).

**Interface** — `export interface UnplaceableJudgement { verdict: UnplaceableVerdict; severity: 'error' | 'warning'; misfits: Array<{ runnerId: string; runnerName: string; reason: MisfitReason }> }`; `export function judgeUnplaceable(input: { job: PlacementJob; scopePaused: boolean; pool: readonly PlacementRunner[]; loads: ReadonlyMap<string, RunnerLoad>; runnerPaused: (runnerId: string) => boolean; now: Date; offlineSec: number }): UnplaceableJudgement | null`.

[unit] jobUnplaceableItems for a QUEUED THREAD row without threadTurn yields no item.
[unit] jobUnplaceableItems for a QUEUED THREAD row with threadTurn and threadsEnabled: false yields an item whose reasons are threads_disabled for every runner.
[unit] jobUnplaceableItems for a QUEUED THREAD row pinned to a runner whose threadCapacity is 1 and which holds one thread yields an item with verdict waiting_capacity.
[unit] jobUnplaceableItems for a QUEUED THREAD row that a runner at protocol 4, with a free thread slot and the backend, can take yields no item.

[integration] With the test Postgres, a QUEUED THREAD job whose turn's backend model no enabled runner offers, queued longer than jobQueuedWarnSec, appears in GET /api/fleet/dashboard attention as job_unplaceable with reason thread_backend for that runner.

userStories.title: Expose computed queued-turn reasons in thread detail
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a read-only queued placement verdict to project and workspace thread detail responses.

**Motivation** — A thread created while its backend was offered can still get stuck later: the runner drops the model, is disabled, or is downgraded.

**Approach** —
- New `PlacementService.queuedVerdict(jobId: string, now: Date, minQueuedSec: number): Promise<QueuedVerdict | null>`, with `interface QueuedVerdict { jobId: string; queuedAt: Date; verdict: UnplaceableVerdict; reasons: Array<{ runnerName: string; reason: MisfitReason }> }`. Read-only: no transaction lock and no write. `null` when the job is missing, not `QUEUED`, or queued for `minQueuedSec` seconds or less, or when `judgeUnplaceable` answers `null`. Otherwise it loads the same inputs `placeJob` loads (repo, pause snapshot, `findPlacementRunners(pinned ? [pinned] : undefined)`, loads, thread assign), builds the job with `toPlacementJob` and `judgedJob`, and calls `judgeUnplaceable`.
- `ChatThreadDetail` (`chat-thread.domain.ts`) gains `queuedTurn: QueuedVerdict | null`. `ThreadsService.get` and `WorkspaceThreadsService.get` set it to `placement.queuedVerdict(activeJob.id, new Date(), config.jobQueuedWarnSec)` when `activeJob?.state === 'QUEUED'`, else `null`. Both services gain a `PlacementService` constructor dependency, appended as the last constructor parameter (already provided in the threads module through `FleetJobsModule`).
- New `QueuedTurnDto` (`apps/api/src/fleet/threads/dto/thread.dto.ts`): `jobId: string`, `queuedAt: string` (ISO), `verdict` (enum of `UnplaceableVerdict` without `fits_not_placed`, which `judgeUnplaceable` never returns), `reasons: QueuedTurnReasonDto[]` (`runnerName`, `reason`). `ThreadDetailDto` gains `@ApiProperty({ type: QueuedTurnDto, nullable: true }) queuedTurn: QueuedTurnDto | null`, which `WorkspaceThreadDetailDto` inherits.

Wire field `queuedTurn` on `GET /api/projects/{slug}/threads/{id}` and `GET /api/threads/{id}`: `null` or `{ "jobId": string, "queuedAt": ISO string, "verdict": "never" | "waiting_capacity" | "runners_paused" | "no_fit" | "no_runners" | "budget_paused", "reasons": [{ "runnerName": string, "reason": MisfitReason }] }`. `PlacementService.queuedVerdict` calls `judgeUnplaceable`; US-003's unit test observes the verdict through `queuedVerdict`, the service entry point. Update every positional construction of both thread services, including thread-mode-change.spec.ts, workspace-turns.spec.ts and thread-flow-preapproval.integration.spec.ts, and preserve the DB-free threads.module.spec.ts compile test. Regenerate `openapi.json` and CLI types with `bun run generate`.

**Scope** — In: nonlocking placement query, thread detail assembly, DTO/contract generation and tests. Out: shared classifier/dashboard extraction (US-002), web rendering/polling (US-004), and writing `FleetJob.stateReason` for a queued THREAD job; the reason is computed on read (dashboard, thread detail).

**Interface** — `PlacementService.queuedVerdict(jobId: string, now: Date, minQueuedSec: number): Promise<QueuedVerdict | null>`; `interface QueuedVerdict { jobId: string; queuedAt: Date; verdict: UnplaceableVerdict; reasons: Array<{ runnerName: string; reason: MisfitReason }> }`; `@ApiProperty({ type: QueuedTurnDto, nullable: true }) queuedTurn: QueuedTurnDto | null`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] PlacementService.queuedVerdict returns null for a job whose state is RUNNING.
[unit] queuedVerdict returns null for a QUEUED job queued 30 s ago with minQueuedSec 60.

[unit] queuedVerdict for a QUEUED THREAD job queued 120 s ago whose only runner misses the turn's backend returns { jobId, queuedAt, verdict: 'no_fit', reasons: [{ runnerName, reason: 'thread_backend' }] }.
[unit] queuedVerdict for a job pinned to runner r1 asks findPlacementRunners for exactly ['r1'].
[unit] queuedVerdict returns null for a QUEUED job queued 120 s ago when one runner fits it.
[unit] ThreadsService.get returns queuedTurn: null without calling queuedVerdict when the thread's activeJob is RUNNING.
[unit] ThreadsService.get with activeJob { id: 'j1', state: 'QUEUED' } calls queuedVerdict with 'j1', a Date and the configured jobQueuedWarnSec, and returns its result as queuedTurn.
[unit] WorkspaceThreadsService.get with a QUEUED activeJob returns the result of queuedVerdict as queuedTurn.

[integration] With the test Postgres, a REPO thread whose QUEUED turn has been queued longer than jobQueuedWarnSec and whose pinned runner no longer offers the backend answers GET /api/projects/:slug/threads/:id with queuedTurn.verdict no_fit and one reason naming that runner with thread_backend.
[integration] The same thread with a turn queued less than jobQueuedWarnSec ago answers queuedTurn: null.
[unit] The committed openapi.json ThreadDetailDto schema has a queuedTurn property referencing QueuedTurnDto, whose properties are exactly jobId, queuedAt, verdict and reasons.
[unit] For a thread without a QUEUED activeJob, ThreadsService.get preserves the existing sendRefusal, handoff and pendingActions values while returning queuedTurn: null.

userStories.title: Show queued-turn reasons on both thread pages
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Render a localized queued-turn notice and refresh detail while a thread's active job remains queued.

**Motivation** — The thread page shows the message as pending with no explanation.

**Approach** —
- `ThreadDetailDto` in `apps/web/lib/thread-types.ts` gains `queuedTurn?: ThreadQueuedTurn | null`, with `ThreadQueuedTurn { jobId: string; queuedAt: string; verdict: string; reasons: { runnerName: string; reason: string }[] }`.
- New `apps/web/components/fleet/threads/ThreadQueuedNotice.vue` (auto-registered as `FleetThreadsThreadQueuedNotice`), prop `thread: ThreadDetailDto`. userStories.title: Advance thread-entry flows past non-question review findings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let THREAD-entry review steps accept minor/answered findings and apply flow-owned PRD edits without editing the thread's spec.

**Motivation** — Each stop needs a person to read the ticket, get the spec fixed, republish, start a new flow and approve it again.

**Approach** —
- `FlowStepAction`'s `dispatch` member (`flow-step-decision.ts:66`) gains `accepted?: FlowFinding[]`.
- `decideFlowStep`, for a COMPLETED SPEC_REVIEW or PRD_REVIEW job with a readable verdict:
  - Baseline: no findings with PRD edits applies them only when `canApplyCalls`; with findings, `!canApplyCalls` stops with `review_ambiguous` (any ambiguous finding) or `review_findings`.
  - Target, no findings: PRD_REVIEW with `prdEdits.length > 0` and `prdEditsJobId !== job.id` returns `apply_prd_edits` (`accepted: []`) whatever `canApplyCalls` is.
  - Target, findings with `canApplyCalls === false` (THREAD entry), in this order:
    1. any `ambiguous` finding: `stop` `review_ambiguous` (unchanged);
    2. more than `FLOW_CALLS_MAX_FINDINGS` findings: `stop` `review_findings` (unchanged);
    3. SPEC_REVIEW: `{ kind: 'dispatch', step: 'PLAN', accepted: verdict.findings }`;
    4. PRD_REVIEW with `prdEdits.length > 0` and `prdEditsJobId !== job.id`: `{ kind: 'apply_prd_edits', jobId, edits: verdict.prdEdits, accepted: verdict.findings }`;
    5. PRD_REVIEW with `prdEditsJobId === job.id`: `{ kind: 'dispatch', step: 'RUN' }` (the findings were recorded with the edits);
    6. PRD_REVIEW otherwise: `{ kind: 'dispatch', step: 'RUN', accepted: verdict.findings }`.
  - `canApplyCalls === true` (NAX entry) is unchanged in every branch.
- `FleetFlowAdvanceService.recordStep(flow, featureId, step, jobId, prNumber?)` (`fleet-flow-advance.service.ts:523`)
  - Target: `recordStep(flow, featureId, step, jobId, prNumber?, accepted?: readonly FlowFinding[])`. When `accepted` is non-empty, the `flow.step` activity payload gains `accepted: accepted.map((f) => truncateFlowText(safeFlowJsonText(f.summary), FLOW_CALL_TEXT_MAX))`, the treatment `advancePrdEdits` gives its accepted findings. The dispatch path (`:126`) passes `action.accepted`.
- `FleetFlowAdvanceService` passes `prdEdits: flow.entry === 'NAX'` to `buildStepDispatch` (`fleet-flow-advance.service.ts:463`). Target: `prdEdits: true`, so a THREAD-entry PRD_REVIEW task also carries `FLOW_PRD_EDITS_INSTRUCTION` (`flow-steps.ts:74`); without it the reviewer never emits edits.
- The RULE and FIX `canApplyCalls` gates (`flow-step-decision.ts:204`, `:231`) are unchanged.

Thread flows pass non-question findings without editing the spec. PRD edits commit to the flow's branch through the existing `FleetFlowCallsService.applyPrdEdits`, whose stale-head guard (head must equal the PLAN result sha) already protects a branch that moved under the flow. Every dispatch still goes through the cost-cap and creator-access guards in the decide pass, so a passing flow never exceeds `costCapUsd`, and no stop (and so no stop ticket) is written for findings the flow handled. koda's verdict classes are only `answered`, `minor` and `ambiguous`; there is no major/blocker class. Update contrary old THREAD assertions in existing decision, advance, calls, PRD edit and integration suites while retaining NAX-entry behavior.

**Scope** — In: review decision algorithm, accepted activity summaries, PRD instructions/commit path and regression assertions. Out: thread placement (US-001–004), rule overrides (US-006–010), writing review spec calls into a thread flow's spec; spec calls stay NAX-entry only; changing the RULE and FIX steps' thread-entry gates; and re-recording accepted findings in crash-recovery recordStep. Sending review findings back to the thread and resuming the flow on the next publish (#426 option 1). A new web view of the flow's accepted findings; they are recorded in the `flow.step` and `flow.prd_edits` activity payloads.

userStories.title: Validate and hash repo rule overrides
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Provide the pure validated input and stable content hash contract for per-repo overrides.

**Motivation** — C11 was deferred on 2026-10-07 until nax could take rules and project context from outside the repo.

**Approach** — US-006 owns `apps/api/src/fleet/repos/rule-override.ts` alone (pure, no database). US-007 owns the model, migration, repository methods, DTOs, service methods, routes, route-command variants, permission key and i18n entry.

- New `apps/api/src/fleet/repos/rule-override.ts`:
  - `RULE_OVERRIDE_LIMITS = { maxFiles: 50, maxFileBytes: 32768, maxTotalBytes: 262144, maxContextBytes: 32768, maxPathLength: 200 }`.
  - `RULE_PATH_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9_-]+(\/[a-z0-9_-]+){0,3}\.md$/` (lowercase only, one to four segments, `.md` file). Lowercase-only keeps two paths from naming one file on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS runners).
  - `validateRuleOverride(raw: unknown): RuleOverrideInput`, with `RuleOverrideInput { rules: { path: string; content: string }[]; rulesMode: 'merge' | 'replace'; context: { content: string; mode: 'append' | 'replace' } | null }`. `rulesMode` defaults to `merge`, `context.mode` to `append`. Refusals throw `ValidationAppException({ reason }, 'fleet.ruleOverride')` (400), with `reason` one of: `rules` (not an array, or more than 50), `path` (fails the pattern or is longer than 200), `duplicatePath`, `content` (not a string, empty, contains NUL, or over 32,768 UTF-8 bytes), `size` (all contents together over 262,144 bytes), `rulesMode`, `context` (not an object, content empty, contains NUL, or over 32,768 bytes), `contextMode`, `empty` (no rules and no context).
  - `ruleOverrideSha256(input: RuleOverrideInput): string`: lowercase hex SHA-256 of `JSON.stringify({ rules: <rules sorted by path>, rulesMode, context })`, so the same content in any order hashes the same.

No database, route or caller. Use the project's exception style; count UTF-8 bytes rather than JavaScript character count. The normalized input is the shared contract consumed by US-007; do not add schema, route DTO, i18n or repository changes in this story.

**Scope** — In: pure rule-override.ts and its colocated unit spec. Out: storage/routes/permission/i18n (US-007), ASSIGN/protocol (US-008), runner validation/materialization (US-009), web form (US-010), and validating rule-file frontmatter or running nax's neutrality lint in koda. Organisation-wide, per-project and per-job rule sets; this feature adds per-repo overrides only.

**Interface** — `RULE_OVERRIDE_LIMITS = { maxFiles: 50, maxFileBytes: 32768, maxTotalBytes: 262144, maxContextBytes: 32768, maxPathLength: 200 }`; `RULE_PATH_PATTERN = /^[a-z0-9_-]+(\/[a-z0-9_-]+){0,3}\.md$/`; `RuleOverrideInput { rules: { path: string; content: string }[]; rulesMode: 'merge' | 'replace'; context: { content: string; mode: 'append' | 'replace' } | null }`; `validateRuleOverride(raw: unknown): RuleOverrideInput`; `ruleOverrideSha256(input: RuleOverrideInput): string`.

userStories.title: Persist and approval-gate per-repo rule overrides
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add globally permissioned REST storage for rule overrides with approval-gated mutation and audited summaries.

**Motivation** — User ruling: its own permission key, `fleet.repo.rules.configure`.

**Approach** — US-006 owns `apps/api/src/fleet/repos/rule-override.ts` alone (pure, no database). US-007 owns the model, migration, repository methods, DTOs, service methods, routes, route-command variants, permission key and i18n entry.

- New Prisma model `FleetRepoRuleOverride` (`apps/api/prisma/schema.prisma`), migration `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261204090000_fleet_repo_rule_override/migration.sql`: `repoId String @id` (relation to `FleetRepo`, `onDelete: Cascade`), `rules Json` (array of `{ path, content }`), `rulesMode String` (`merge` | `replace`), `contextContent String?`, `contextMode String?` (`append` | `replace`), `ruleFiles Int`, `sha256 String`, `updatedById String`, `updatedByType String`, `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt`. `FleetRepo` gains `ruleOverride FleetRepoRuleOverride?`.
- `IFleetRepoRepository` gains `findRuleOverride(repoId): Promise<FleetRepoRuleOverrideRecord | null>`, `upsertRuleOverride(repoId, input, sha256, actor)` and `deleteRuleOverride(repoId): Promise<boolean>`. `FleetRepoRecord` gains optional `ruleOverride?: RuleOverrideSummary | null`, with `RuleOverrideSummary { sha256: string; ruleFiles: number; rulesMode: 'merge' | 'replace'; contextMode: 'append' | 'replace' | null; updatedAt: Date }`, read by `list` and `findById` from the row's scalar columns (`sha256`, `ruleFiles`, `rulesMode`, `contextMode`, `updatedAt`), never from the `rules` Json, so listing repos does not load rule bodies.
- `FleetRepoDto` gains `ruleOverride: RuleOverrideSummaryDto | null` (`updatedAt` as ISO string), from `FleetRepoDto.from` (absent gives `null`).
- `FleetReposService` gains `getRuleOverride(id)`, `setRuleOverride(principal, id, raw)` and `clearRuleOverride(principal, id)`. Set and clear run in `txManager.run`: unknown repo gives `NotFoundAppException({}, 'fleet.repos')`; set validates, hashes, upserts and records an audit entry `{ key: 'fleet.repo.rules.configure', resourceType: 'fleet-repo', resourceId: id, projectId, summary: 'rule override set (<n> files, <rulesMode>)' }`; clear deletes and records `summary: 'rule override cleared'` only when a row existed. Set and clear both return the updated `FleetRepoDto` (with its `ruleOverride` summary); `getRuleOverride` returns the full `RuleOverrideDto` (`rules`, `rulesMode`, `context`, `sha256`, `updatedAt`) or `null`.
- `FleetReposController` gains `GET :id/rule-override` (`@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)`, `@Requires('fleet.repo.rules.configure')`, not approval-gated, returns `RuleOverrideDto` or `null`, because it returns full rule bodies), `PUT :id/rule-override` and `DELETE :id/rule-override` (both `@HttpCode(200)`, `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)`, `@Requires('fleet.repo.rules.configure')`, `@ApprovalGated()`, mirroring `configureFixUnprotected`), with Swagger responses 200/202/400/403/404. The PUT handler calls `validateRuleOverride(body)` before `routeGate.run`, so an invalid body answers 400 and never becomes an approval request; the service validates again at execution.
- `FLEET_REPO_ROUTE_VARIANTS` gains `ruleOverrideSet: 'rest:fleet-repos.rule-override.set'` and `ruleOverrideClear: 'rest:fleet-repos.rule-override.clear'`; `FleetRepoRouteCommands.onModuleInit` registers both for `fleet.repo.rules.configure`.
- `NEW_KEY_SCOPES` (`catalog.ts:126`) gains `'fleet.repo.rules.configure': 'global'` (high risk through the `fleet.repo.` prefix, so an agent caller waits for a human by default).
- i18n `apps/api/src/i18n/{en,zh}/fleet.json` gain a `ruleOverride` entry with `"-2"` and `"400"` messages naming `{reason}`, as `threads.json` `input` does.

`setRuleOverride` calls `validateRuleOverride` and `ruleOverrideSha256`; US-007's integration ACs prove the route refuses what the validator refuses and stores the hash it computes. The web sends `PUT /fleet/repos/{id}/rule-override` with JSON body `{ "rules": [{ "path": "api.md", "content": "..." }], "rulesMode": "merge", "context": { "content": "...", "mode": "append" } }` (context may be `null`), `DELETE` with no body; both answer `FleetRepoDto` (or an approval request). It reads `GET` as `RuleOverrideDto` or `null`, and reads `ruleOverride` from `FleetRepoDto`. Use existing AuditRecorder and envelope patterns. Add RuleOverrideDto and RuleOverrideSummaryDto alongside FleetRepoDto in the existing dto/fleet-repo.dto.ts. Update route-command variants 6->8, NEW_KEY_SCOPES expectations, regenerate role-matrix snapshot/cell count 245->246, gated-operation count 146->148, OpenAPI/admin gate tables, and regenerate `openapi.json` and CLI types with `bun run generate`. Do not load rule bodies for repo summaries or inherit the unrelated GitHub-only fix-unprotected constraint.

**Scope** — In: table/relation/migration, repositories/DTOs/services, approval/RBAC/audit/i18n/routes and contract regeneration. Out: changing pure validator ownership (US-006), job snapshot/ASSIGN (US-008), runner materialization (US-009), admin dialog (US-010), CLI/assistant/MCP tools, permission inventory TSV changes and extra route rate limiting beyond the global throttler. userStories.description:
**Goal** — Snapshot the current per-repo override at nax job assignment and retain its summary on the job.

**Motivation** — Designer calls (user asked for them, 2026-11-10): rule sets are per repo only; the override is read when the job is assigned, like `fixTrustDetectedChecks`.

**Approach** —
- `AssignPayload` (`packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts`, types only) gains `ruleOverride?: RuleOverrideAssign`, with `RuleOverrideAssign { sha256: string; rulesMode: 'merge' | 'replace'; rules: { path: string; content: string }[]; context?: { content: string; mode: 'append' | 'replace' } }`, documented as present only on RUN, PLAN, REVIEW, FIX and AGENT.
- `IFleetJobRepository` gains `findRuleOverride(repoId): Promise<RuleOverrideAssign | null>` and `setRuleOverrideSummary(jobId, summary: JobRuleOverrideSummary | null): Promise<void>`, with `JobRuleOverrideSummary { sha256: string; ruleFiles: number; rulesMode: 'merge' | 'replace'; contextMode: 'append' | 'replace' | null }`.
- `FleetJob` gains `ruleOverride Json?`, migration `apps/api/prisma/migrations/20261204100000_fleet_job_rule_override/migration.sql`. `FleetJobRecord` gains optional `ruleOverride?: JobRuleOverrideSummary | null` (absent means none), like `prRulings?`, so existing record literals stay valid.
- `buildAssignPayload(job, repo, cloneUrl, gitIdentity, thread?)` (`apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/assign-payload.ts:28`)
  - Target: `buildAssignPayload(job, repo, cloneUrl, gitIdentity, thread?, ruleOverride?: RuleOverrideAssign | null)`; spreads `{ ruleOverride }` when it is non-null and `job.command` is one of RUN, PLAN, REVIEW, FIX, AGENT. Otherwise the key is absent.
- `PlacementService.assign` (`placement.service.ts:263`)
  - Target: for those five commands it reads `this.repo.findRuleOverride(job.repoId)` inside the placement transaction, passes it to `buildAssignPayload`, and calls `setRuleOverrideSummary(job.id, summaryOf(override))` (`null` when there is none) right after `casAssign` and before `findById`, so the `after` record that `buildAssignPayload` and `transitions.record` use already carries the summary. THREAD and config-kind jobs read nothing and write nothing.
- `FleetJobDto` gains `@ApiPropertyOptional({ nullable: true }) ruleOverride: JobRuleOverrideSummaryDto | null` from `FleetJobDto.from`.

The rule override travels with the ASSIGN, not a separate fetch, so a readopted job runs with the override it was assigned. Turning an override off or changing it affects jobs assigned after the change. Mixed versions: an older runner drops the unknown `ruleOverride` field (its parser copies an allow-list) and runs with the repo's own rules. An older API never sends it. The job's `ruleOverride` therefore records what was assigned, not proof that nax applied it. The `FleetRepoRuleOverride` row written by `setRuleOverride` is what `findRuleOverride` reads at assignment; US-008's integration ACs store it through the US-007 route. Wire field `ruleOverride` at the top level of the ASSIGN command payload: `{ "sha256": 64-hex string, "rulesMode": "merge" | "replace", "rules": [{ "path": string, "content": string }], "context"?: { "content": string, "mode": "append" | "replace" } }`. The job page reads `ruleOverride` from `FleetJobDto` as `null` or `{ "sha256", "ruleFiles", "rulesMode", "contextMode" }`. Use import type only for the shared protocol in API code. Add JobRuleOverrideSummaryDto alongside FleetJobDto in the existing jobs/dto/fleet-job.dto.ts; extend placement mock repositories for nax commands and regenerate OpenAPI/CLI contracts.

**Scope** — In: shared wire type, job JSON migration/record/DTO, repository mapping, assignment transaction and payload integration. Out: override configuration storage/routes (US-007), runner parser/profile changes (US-009), job summary UI (US-010), applying an override to CONFIG jobs or threads, copying the override into the run bundle and adding a runner capability.

**Interface** — `RuleOverrideAssign { sha256: string; rulesMode: 'merge' | 'replace'; rules: { path: string; content: string }[]; context?: { content: string; mode: 'append' | 'replace' } }`; `findRuleOverride(repoId): Promise<RuleOverrideAssign | null>`; `setRuleOverrideSummary(jobId, summary: JobRuleOverrideSummary | null): Promise<void>`; `JobRuleOverrideSummary { sha256: string; ruleFiles: number; rulesMode: 'merge' | 'replace'; contextMode: 'append' | 'replace' | null }`; `buildAssignPayload(job, repo, cloneUrl, gitIdentity, thread?, ruleOverride?: RuleOverrideAssign | null)`.

userStories.title: Materialize assigned overrides into per-job nax profiles
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Validate assigned overrides and hand private job-directory rules/context to every supported nax job through its profile.

**Motivation** — koda passes none (`buildNaxArgv`, `apps/runner/src/executor/nax-process.ts`).

**Approach** —
- `parseAssign` (`apps/runner/src/supervisor/assign-parser.ts`)
  - Target: a top-level `ruleOverride` is accepted only on RUN, PLAN, REVIEW, FIX and AGENT. It must be an object with `sha256` (64 lowercase hex), `rulesMode` (`merge`|`replace`), `rules` (array of at most 50 `{ path, content }`, path matching `^[a-z0-9_-]+(\/[a-z0-9_-]+){0,3}\.md$`, content a string), and an optional `context` (`{ content: string, mode: 'append' | 'replace' }`). It is copied into the cleaned assign. Any other shape, or the key on another command, fails with `bad('ruleOverride')`.
- New `apps/runner/src/executor/rule-override.ts`: `materializeRuleOverride(jobDir: string, override: RuleOverrideAssign): Promise<JobProfileContext>`, with `JobProfileContext { rules: { overrideDir: string; overrideMode: 'merge' | 'replace' }; projectContext?: { file: string; mode: 'append' | 'replace' } }`. It removes `<jobDir>/koda-rules` and `<jobDir>/koda-context.md` first, writes every rule to `<jobDir>/koda-rules/<path>` (directories 0700, files 0600), writes `context.content` to `<jobDir>/koda-context.md` when present, and returns absolute paths. A path that resolves outside `<jobDir>/koda-rules` throws `Error('rule override path')`.
- `jobProfileContent(outputDir, projectName, relay?, botCostLimitUsd?, modelAliases?)` and `writeJobProfile(...)` (`job-profile.ts:31`, `:48`)
  - Target: both gain a last optional `context?: JobProfileContext`. When present, the profile JSON gains `context: { rules: { overrideDir, overrideMode }, projectContext?: { file, mode } }`; when absent the profile is unchanged.
- `HostExecutor.prepare` (`host-executor.ts:115`) and `HostExecutor.spawnFixStep` (`:212`): when `assign.ruleOverride` is present, call `materializeRuleOverride(jobDir, assign.ruleOverride)` and pass the result to `writeJobProfile`. `prepareConfigJob` and thread hosting are unchanged.

The override reaches nax through the per-job profile (`writeJobProfile`, `apps/runner/src/executor/job-profile.ts:48`) rather than argv, so every nax command the job runs (`run`, `plan`, `bot review`, `bot fix`, `agents run`) gets it; CONFIG jobs and threads never do. `.nax/` rule files are never edited by this feature. The override lives in the job directory only. The rule override travels with the ASSIGN, not a separate fetch, so a readopted job runs with the override it was assigned. Turning an override off or changing it affects jobs assigned after the change. The existing parser's `bad('ruleOverride')` serializes detail `invalid ruleOverride`; retain that convention. CONFIG denotes the config-job family here: packages/fleet-protocol/src/config-jobs.ts defines CONFIG_EDIT and CONFIG_DRIFT, not a new literal CONFIG command. A materialization Error('rule override path') propagates into HostExecutor.prepare's existing reasonFromError mapping as { ok: false, reason: 'workspace: rule override path' }; do not change generic prepare error formatting. Check all rule destinations before writing any rule so a malicious outside path writes no file. Preserve relay, bot cost, model aliases and atomic 0600 profile writing; the FIX second profile write must also include context. Use real temp files and injected naxHome in tests, not the installed nax.

**Scope** — In: cleaned wire validation, private materialization, optional profile overlay and prepare/FIX integration. Out: API override storage/snapshot (US-007/008), web admin (US-010), applying to CONFIG or threads, adding argv flags, a runner capability for rule overrides, copying overrides into bundles or editing checkout .nax rules/context.

**Interface** — `materializeRuleOverride(jobDir: string, override: RuleOverrideAssign): Promise<JobProfileContext>`; `JobProfileContext { rules: { overrideDir: string; overrideMode: 'merge' | 'replace' }; projectContext?: { file: string; mode: 'append' | 'replace' } }`; `context?: JobProfileContext` as the last optional argument to `jobProfileContent` and `writeJobProfile`; malformed assignments fail with `bad('ruleOverride')`.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Provide the globally permissioned rule-override dialog and display which override a job was assigned.

**Motivation** — A registered repo can carry a rule override: rule files laid out like `.nax/rules/`, an optional project-context file, and nax's combine modes.

**Approach** —
- `FleetRepo` (`apps/web/lib/fleet-types.ts`) gains `ruleOverride: FleetRuleOverrideSummary | null`; `FleetJobDto` (`fleet-types.ts:295`) gains `ruleOverride?: FleetJobRuleOverride | null`; new `FleetRuleOverride` (full body).

The last two return `{ kind: 'pending', request }` when the answer has `permissionKey`, else `{ kind: 'saved', repo }` with the returned `FleetRepo`.
- New `apps/web/components/fleet/RepoRuleOverrideDialog.vue` (`FleetRepoRuleOverrideDialog`), prop `repo: FleetRepo`. A button `data-testid="fleet-repo-rules-<owner>-<name>"` labelled `fleet.repos.ruleOverride.open` (with the file count when `repo.ruleOverride` is set) opens a dialog that loads the override with `getRuleOverride`. It shows one row per rule file (path input, content textarea, remove button), an add-file button, a `rulesMode` select (merge, replace), a context textarea and a context-mode select (append, replace), plus Save and Clear buttons, all disabled without `fleet.repo.rules.configure` in the global permissions. Save sends `{ rules: [{ path, content }], rulesMode, context: { content, mode } | null }` (context `null` when the textarea is empty). A pending answer shows `fleet.repos.ruleOverride.pending`; a failure shows `extractApiError(err)` in `role="alert"`; a saved answer emits `saved` with the returned repo, which the page puts in its `repos` list, so the button's file count follows.
- `apps/web/pages/admin/fleet/repos.vue` mounts it in the actions cell for every repo.
- `apps/web/pages/[project]/fleet/jobs/[id]/index.vue` shows `data-testid="fleet-job-rule-override"` when `job.ruleOverride` is set: `fleet.jobs.ruleOverride.summary` (worded as the override the job was assigned) with `{files}`, `{mode}`, `{context}` and the first 8 characters of `sha256`.

The job page reads `ruleOverride` from `FleetJobDto` as `null` or `{ "sha256", "ruleFiles", "rulesMode", "contextMode" }`. GitLab is supported; do not copy the GitHub-only visibility restriction of unrelated repo switches. The assigned summary is not proof an older runner applied it.

**Scope** — In: web types/composable/dialog/actions integration, saved/pending/errors, job assignment summary, locales and Jest tests.
